title: Ants on a Stick
statement: $25$ ants are placed independently and uniformly on a stick of length $1$ metre. Each faces left or right at random, and all walk at $1$ metre per minute. When two ants meet, both turn around instantly. An ant leaves when it walks off an end. What is the expected time, in minutes, until the stick is empty?
insight: A collision where both ants turn around looks exactly like the ants passing through each other. So the stick empties when the last ghost ant walks off, each ghost needing a uniform(0,1) time.
hints: If you couldn't tell the ants apart, what would a collision look like?
Pretend ants pass through each other. Then each ant walks straight off an end.
Each ant's time to its end is uniform on $[0,1]$. What is the expected maximum of 25 such times?
solution:
Ignoring labels, two ants bouncing off each other look the same as two ants passing through. So the set of ant positions evolves as if they pass through. Each "ghost" walks straight off, taking time equal to its distance to the end it faces, which is uniform on $[0,1]$ and independent across ants.

The stick empties at the maximum of 25 independent uniforms: $E = \tfrac{25}{26}$.
